svg.aria-label: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop — interactive learning interface with flower diagram, word bank, instructions, hint, check-answer and reset popups
svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: A static, self-contained SVG that simulates a drag-and-drop labeling exercise: label the ten parts of a flower using the word bank. Hint, Check Answer and Reset buttons open hidden popup panels toggled with internal links and CSS :target visibility.

g.text: Label the ten parts of the flower
Fig. 1 — A complete, lily-style flower with the ovary cut open to reveal the ovules. Match each numbered slot to a word-bank tile.
Look at the ten numbered slots around the flower diagram.
Drag a label tile from the word bank onto the matching slot.
Press Check Answer to reveal the key and your score.
Use Hint when stuck, or Reset to send every tile back.
Female parts — pistil, stigma, style, ovary
Pollen lands on the stickystigma of the same species.
A pollen tube grows downthe style toward the ovary.
Fertilized ovules becomeseeds; the ovary → a fruit.
Fig. 2 — Pollination and fertilization, simplified. No pollen, no seeds!
WORD BANK — DRAG EACH LABEL ONTO ITS NUMBERED SLOT
Stuck? Click Hint, Check Answer or Reset in the guide panel.

g.text: Static SVG simulation — popups open via in-document links and CSS :target toggles. No JavaScript, no images, no external assets.
Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop · Botany Unit · Lesson 3.2
Three nudges before you peek at the answer key.
Colours match the systems: pink = female, amber = male, green = support.
Top slot: the sticky stigma catches pollen grains.
Thick base under the petals — the receptacle anchors everything.
Small green leaf under each petal — that's a sepal.
Amber trio: stamen (6) = whole unit; anther (3) + filament (4) = its parts.
Pink quartet: pistil (2) = stigma (1) + style (8) + ovary (7).
How did your board compare? Green ticks show the correct labels.
All ten labels have been returned to the word bank.
Tip: press Hint for three gentle nudges before peeking at the key.
